clue.text: Before noon accountant is duty-bound to be free

indicators.note: the duty is bound around the other letters, enclosing them like a binding strap

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a duty charged on goods

indicators.note: the accountant is placed before noon in the run of letters

parts.note: ACA, Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, is an accountant's qualification
N is the abbreviation for noon, the midday point on a clock face

explanation.surface: An accountant is obliged to be off work by midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts ACA ahead of N, and 'duty-bound' then wraps VAT around ACAN, so 'free' is left as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Free and vacant both describe something unoccupied, such as a seat or a room.

clue.text: Semi-nude model without turnover of work that's money in the bank

indicators.note: half of the word nude is taken, its second half
turnover means the abbreviation for a work is flipped round

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A half-naked model posing without the work being turned over, earning money for the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means outside: the reversed work stands outside, ahead of, the model. 'Semi-' takes the back half of the word, and 'turnover of' flips the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a sum of money placed in a bank account.

clue.text: Small white wine cocktail in San Tropez starts a fashion

parts.note: mini means small, as in a mini car

indicators.note: the cocktail goes inside the opening letters of the French resort's name
the starts of San and Tropez are their first letters

parts.note: kir is white wine mixed with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A drink served on the Riviera starts a new trend.
explanation.definitionFit: The short skirt was a famous fashion of the 1960s.

clue.text: Misinformation about red fruit

indicators.note: the misinformation goes about, around, the revolutionary

parts.note: a lie is deliberate misinformation
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, is a crossword 'red'

explanation.surface: False claims made about some red fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' is not a colour of the fruit; it is the communist Che.
explanation.definitionFit: A lychee, also spelt this way, is a small Chinese fruit with white flesh.

clue.text: What a lazy setter may resort to

definitions.text: What a lazy setter may resort to

parts.words: What a lazy setter may resort to
parts.note: the setter is not a puzzle compiler but a dog of the setter breed, whose resort is its shelter

explanation.surface: A dig at crossword compilers who take shortcuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's shelter is where an idle hound would retreat to rest.

clue.text: Abandon anorak and go for jumper

indicators.note: to do something with abandon is to do it wildly, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Throw off your coat and put on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a British sweater, as suggested by 'anorak', but it means an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial moves by leaping on its hind legs, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Oddly least pain that comes up is to do with birth

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards
the odd letters of least pain are taken: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: The least pain possible during a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters give LATAN, which 'that comes up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective meaning relating to birth, as in prenatal care.

clue.text: Caught hem needs repair

indicators.note: a repair puts things into a new order, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snagged hem must be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshed means tangled in a net, so caught.

clue.text: A half of Pernod and vermouth provided drink

indicators.note: the first half of the drink's name is taken

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: Ordering a mix of pastis and vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Smallest particle visible in any dissection

indicators.note: the particle can be seen inside the word any, which surrounds it

parts.note: an atom was once thought the smallest particle of matter

explanation.surface: A microscopic particle shows up whenever something is cut apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy literally means cutting up, the dissection of a body to study it.

clue.text: First-class oil used for garlic mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written here with I for the 1

indicators.note: the oil is used, worked over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The best oil goes into making a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is the Provençal sauce of garlic and egg yolk emulsified with oil.

clue.text: Found a woozy bliss following electric shock treatment

indicators.note: the run of letters comes after the treatment

parts.note: EST is electroshock therapy, electric shock treatment

indicators.note: a woozy, tipsy speaker slurs the final hiss of bliss into a shushing sound

explanation.surface: Someone found a dizzy happiness after their shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woozy' turns BLISS into the drunken BLISH, the final S slurred to SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company is to set it up, to bring it into being.

clue.text: Pen with a lot of style

indicators.note: a lot of the word style is most of it, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Writing with plenty of flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the farmyard sense: a pen is an enclosure for livestock, and the pigs' enclosure goes by this short name.

clue.text: Dunces' stream the customary form for rugby forwards?

parts.note: thick means stupid, the quality of dunces
a set is a school stream, a class grouped by ability

explanation.surface: Pupils in the bottom class, the usual lot to end up in the scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as THICK SET, a class of dunces; whole, it describes the stocky build of rugby forwards, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby forwards are typically stocky and heavily built, the build being described.

clue.text: Ocelot's first and second target is a raptor

indicators.note: the first of Ocelot's is its opening letter

parts.note: prey is the target of a hunter

explanation.surface: A wild cat has its eye on a target in a wildlife scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, which is what raptor means.

clue.text: Tramp's wearing outfit that wouldn't have looked out of place in the Apollo

definitions.text: that wouldn't have looked out of place in the Apollo

indicators.note: the tramp's steps are inside the outfit, as a wearer is inside clothes

parts.note: a suit is an outfit of clothes
tramp is paces, to tramp being to march or pace

explanation.surface: A vagrant in a costume that would suit a space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: Apollo was the NASA moon programme, not the London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts on the Apollo missions wore pressurised suits for space.

clue.text: Wag is somewhat akin to comedian?

parts.note: Russell Brand is a British comedian
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: Is a joker much like a stand-up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wag' looks like a joker, matching the comedian; it is the verb, to wave something about.
explanation.definitionFit: To wag something is to wave it, as one would brandish a sword.

clue.text: Peruse missing article by premier in tabloid

indicators.note: the article goes missing, taken out of the word for peruse

parts.note: to read is to peruse
A is the indefinite article
top means premier, first in rank

explanation.surface: Reading a gossip piece about the Prime Minister in a scandal sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Red top is British slang for a tabloid paper, from the red mastheads of the Sun and Mirror.

clue.text: Land right in the middle of green with meanest shot

indicators.note: the middle letter of green is its central E
shot means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's poor stroke lands on the middle of the green.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture of a green and a bad shot hides a legal term; 'shot' scrambles MEANEST into ASEMENT, which follows the green's middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An easement is a legal right over another's land, such as a right of way.

clue.text: See 17
A 'kosher' ratatouille's ingredients generating a list of corrections

indicators.note: the answer's letters are among the contents of these words

explanation.surface: A kosher vegetable stew whose ingredients come with a list of fixes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are corrections listed in a printed book.

clue.text: Something very difficult in 12?

definitions.meaning: a ... of a job is a very difficult task
the animal kept in a pen like the answer at 12

explanation.definitionFit: A pig is British slang for a hard task, and the farm animal lives in a sty.

clue.text: France changing rule for popular subsidy

indicators.note: the letter for rule is changed for the word for popular

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: France altering its policy on a popular grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means money provided, so a subsidy funds something.

clue.text: Rest during fighting

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
action is fighting, combat

explanation.surface: Respite in the midst of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it means fighting; whole, it means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a lack of activity, a state of rest.

clue.text: Sailor depressed by Birmingham's centre gets delicious drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, being pressed down under means coming below

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor in Birmingham finds a fine drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' is not the middle letter; it is the NEC, Birmingham's big exhibition venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods, so any delicious drink.

clue.text: Monster is seen swimming

indicators.note: swimming means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monster is seen swimming in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loch Ness monster in Scotland is affectionately named this.

clue.text: Wok legend cooked for acquaintance

indicators.note: cooked means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writing a recipe for a celebrated wok dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquaintance with a subject is familiarity with it, knowing about it.

clue.text: Review a verifiable case for change

indicators.note: the words are a casing for the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: Calling for a check on a provable argument for change.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to vacillate, to keep changing one's mind.

clue.text: George Raft's Colombo a match for petty quarrels

definitions.meaning: the gangster played by George Raft in the film Some Like It Hot, nicknamed for his ankle gaiters

explanation.definitionFit: Spats are small quarrels, and Spats Colombo was the gangster in Some Like It Hot.

clue.text: More than half of vivisections performed in regular clothes

indicators.note: performed means worked over, so those letters are rearranged
more than half the word means its opening seven letters

explanation.surface: Lab procedures carried out by scientists out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Civvies is slang for civilian clothes, worn instead of uniform.

clue.text: Street musician's extraordinary charisma drawing one in as sun comes out

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
drawing marks the start of the swap: a letter is drawn in
in completes the drawing in of the letter for one
comes out marks the sun's letter leaving the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A busker's charm draws a crowd as the sun appears.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHARISMA, I replaces S to give CHARIMAI, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi bands are Mexican street musicians.

clue.text: Craving designer T-shirt

indicators.note: a designer remakes things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Longing for a branded top.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is a strong craving or longing.
